title: Valencia/Tapper/Estius: Trent defined species-same faith without charity; number-same is certain but not defined
source_text: XIV. Ista docet inter alios Gregorius de Valentia. Primo enim probat eandem fidem posse esse tum formatam per charitatem, tum etiam informem; Constat, inquit, ea quae non pertinent ad essentiam rei, sed rei accidunt, non multiplicare ipsam, cum potest eadem res variis accidentibus subesse; sed quod fides per charitatem sit formata, aut non sit, accidit ei, nec ad ipsius essentiam per se pertinet. Postea vero observat ex fide certum esse quod eadem fides vera secundum speciem constare possit cum charitate & sine charitate, quod vero etiam eadem numero non esse ex fide certum. Neque fuit, inquit, in Concilio Tridentino de hoc controversia adversus haereticos, sed solum voluerunt Patres statuere, quod fides etiam vera Catholica & Theologica possit esse sine charitate, & reipsa sit in peccatoribus fidelibus. Non autem definierunt quod etiam eadem numero. Subjungit tamen id jam adeo certum esse, ut communiter Theologi sentiant, oppositum esse temerarium, eo quod repugnet in re gravi communi Doctorum sententiae. Tom. 3. in Summam Thomae, Disput. 1. quaest. 4. puncto 4. Quibus consentit Ruardus Tapperus; postquam enim conclusit tanquam de fide certum, quod eadem fides secundum speciem maneat sine charitate; addit, Perisimile etiam esse, quod eadem quoque numero maneat. Tom. 2. art. 8. pag. 64. Et idem etiam observat Estius loco supra citato.
pass_a_gloss: These things Gregory of Valencia teaches among others. For first he proves that the same faith can be both formed through charity and also unformed; It is agreed, he says, that those things which do not pertain to the essence of a thing, but happen to the thing, do not multiply the thing itself, since the same thing can be subject to various accidents; but that faith is formed through charity, or is not, happens to it, and does not of itself pertain to its essence. Afterward he observes that it is certain from the faith that the same true faith according to species can stand with charity and without charity, but that it is also the same in number is not certain from the faith. Nor was there, he says, in the Council of Trent a controversy about this against the heretics, but the Fathers only wished to establish that even true Catholic and Theological faith can be without charity, and in reality is in faithful sinners. But they did not define that it is also the same in number. Yet he adds that this is now so certain that theologians commonly think the opposite is rash, because it conflicts in a grave matter with the common sentence of the Doctors. Tom. 3 on the Summa of Thomas, Disputation 1, question 4, point 4. With which Ruardus Tapper agrees; for after he concluded as certain of the faith that the same faith according to species remains without charity; he adds that it is also very like that it remains the same also in number. Tom. 2, article 8, page 64. And Estius also observes the same in the place cited above.
pass_b_english: Valencia: accidents do not multiply the essence — formed or not is accidental to faith — so same-species faith with or without charity is of the faith.
Trent settled against heretics that true Catholic theological faith can exist without charity in faithful sinners; it did not define numerical identity.
Numerical sameness is now so common that the opposite is called rash; Tapper and Estius concur that species-sameness is de fide and number-sameness highly probable.
